templates.pattern: A person has a mass of [M] kg and a height of [H] m. Calculate their Body Mass Index (BMI).
templates.explanation:
BMI = mass ÷ height²
= [M] ÷ [H]²
= [M] ÷ [H*H]
= [RESULT]

BMI ranges: underweight < 18.5, healthy 18.5-24.9, overweight 25-29.9, obese ≥ 30. BMI is a useful screening tool but does not account for muscle mass or body composition.

templates.pattern: A person has a heart rate of [HR] beats per minute and a stroke volume of [SV] mL per beat. Calculate the cardiac output in mL per minute.
templates.explanation:
Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume
= [HR] × [SV]
= [RESULT] mL/min

Resting cardiac output is approximately 5000 mL/min. During vigorous exercise it can increase to 20,000-25,000 mL/min in trained athletes.

templates.pattern: A person has a cardiac output of [CO] mL/min and a stroke volume of [SV] mL per beat. Calculate the heart rate in beats per minute.
templates.explanation:
Heart rate = cardiac output ÷ stroke volume
= [CO] ÷ [SV]
= [RESULT] beats/min

Normal resting heart rate is 60-100 beats per minute. Athletes often have lower resting heart rates because their hearts pump more blood per beat.

templates.pattern: A person has a cardiac output of [CO] mL/min and a heart rate of [HR] beats per minute. Calculate the stroke volume in mL per beat.
templates.explanation:
Stroke volume = cardiac output ÷ heart rate
= [CO] ÷ [HR]
= [RESULT] mL/beat

Stroke volume increases during exercise due to increased venous return (Frank-Starling mechanism). Trained athletes have larger stroke volumes even at rest.

templates.pattern: A person takes [B] breaths in [T] minutes. Calculate the breathing rate in breaths per minute.
templates.explanation:
Breathing rate = number of breaths ÷ time
= [B] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] breaths/min

Normal resting breathing rate is 12-20 breaths per minute. During exercise it increases to meet the greater oxygen demand and remove excess CO₂.

templates.pattern: A person has a pulmonary ventilation rate of [VR] mL/min and a breathing rate of [BR] breaths per minute. Calculate the tidal volume in mL.
templates.explanation:
Tidal volume = pulmonary ventilation rate ÷ breathing rate
= [VR] ÷ [BR]
= [RESULT] mL

Tidal volume is the volume of air inhaled or exhaled in one normal breath. At rest it is approximately 500 mL. It increases significantly during exercise.

templates.pattern: A person has a breathing rate of [BR] breaths per minute and a tidal volume of [TV] mL. Calculate the pulmonary ventilation rate in mL per minute.
templates.explanation:
Pulmonary ventilation rate = breathing rate × tidal volume
= [BR] × [TV]
= [RESULT] mL/min

Pulmonary ventilation rate measures the total volume of air moved per minute. At rest it is about 6000 mL/min and can exceed 100,000 mL/min during intense exercise.

templates.pattern: A patient has a systolic blood pressure of [SYS] mmHg and a diastolic blood pressure of [DIA] mmHg. Calculate the pulse pressure in mmHg.
templates.explanation:
Pulse pressure = systolic pressure − diastolic pressure
= [SYS] − [DIA]
= [RESULT] mmHg

Normal pulse pressure is 40-60 mmHg. A wide pulse pressure may indicate aortic regurgitation or atherosclerosis. A narrow pulse pressure may indicate heart failure or shock.

templates.pattern: A person consumes [IN] kcal per day and expends [EXP] kcal per day through activity and metabolism. Calculate the daily calorie balance in kcal.
templates.explanation:
Calorie balance = intake − expenditure
= [IN] − [EXP]
= [RESULT] kcal

A positive balance means more energy is consumed than used — the excess is stored as fat. A deficit of 3500 kcal is roughly equivalent to losing 0.45 kg of body fat.

templates.pattern: A drug has a half life of [THALF] hours. The initial concentration is [C0] mg/L. Calculate the concentration remaining after [N] half lives in mg/L.
templates.explanation:
Drug concentration = C₀ × (0.5)ⁿ
= [C0] × (0.5)^[N]
= [C0] × [pow(0.5,N)]
= [RESULT] mg/L

Drug concentration falls by half with each half life. After 5 half lives less than 3% of the original dose remains — the drug is considered eliminated from the body.
